👤 Roger Seheult, MD (39.6K) 🗓27m 👁️847
Pneumonic plague—key facts: Symptoms usually begin 1–3 days after exposure (sometimes up to 7). R₀ estimates vary: about 1.2 in historical U.S. data and 2.4 in a model of Madagascar’s 2017 outbreak. It spreads through respiratory droplets, especially during close contact. If suspected, start antibiotics immediately—do not wait for test results; treatment within the first 24 hours of symptoms is critical. In historical published cases, the death rate was about 17% with antibiotics (pooled estimate; timing and care varied), versus nearly 100% without treatment. Untreated disease can become fatal within 18–24 hours of symptom onset.

Reports about the Irkutsk case are still developing, so I’d describe it as suspected/reported pneumonic plague unless officials confirm the diagnosis.

Mindshare (16) 🗓22h 👁️325
How can creator fees be used to increase attention and popularity of a coin?

Before answering that, we want to take a step back and explain why we built Mindshare.

Crypto has become extremely good at launching tokens. A name, an image and a community can become a liquid market in minutes. Solana made that process faster than anything that came before it.

But once the token is live, almost every project runs into the same question:

What is all that activity actually building?

Right now, creator fees usually end up in one of a few places.

The creator’s wallet.
The standard model. Every trade produces revenue for the person who launched the token, but holders have no control over how that money is used—or whether it is used for the community at all.

Token buybacks.
The most common attempt at giving fees back to holders. Buybacks can support the token, but they do not create anything outside the chart. The community still needs a reason to exist when trading slows... Show more
